title_en: Shenzhen Mou Technology Co., Ltd. v. Shenzhen Mou Electronic Technology Development Co., Ltd. et al. — dispute over infringement of utility model patent
ruling_gist_en: 1. Where a property preservation measure taken against the patent in question leads to the suspension of the patent invalidation procedure, with the result that the China National Intellectual Property Administration fails to issue a review decision on the request for invalidation before the judgment in the patent infringement lawsuit is rendered, the people's court may, in light of the specific circumstances of the case, make appropriate arrangements for the performance of the obligations determined in the judgment, including attaching necessary conditions to the performance of items such as cessation of infringement and damages. For example, it may take the review decision made by the China National Intellectual Property Administration upholding the validity of the patent claim on which the patentee relies for the lawsuit as a prerequisite for the performance of the judgment items, and make corresponding arrangements for interest on debts during the period, so as to reasonably balance the interests of all parties.

full_text_en:
Shenzhen Mou Technology Co., Ltd. v. Shenzhen Mou Electronic Technology Development Co., Ltd. et al. — Dispute over Infringement of Utility Model Patent

[Ruling Summary]

1. Where the patent invalidation proceeding is suspended due to the adoption of property preservation measures against the patent in question, so that the China National Intellectual Property Administration fails to issue an examination decision on the invalidation request before the judgment in the patent infringement action is rendered, the people's court may, based on the specific circumstances of the case, make appropriate arrangements for the performance of the obligations determined in the judgment, including attaching necessary conditions to the performance of items such as cessation of infringement and compensation for losses. For example, the effective examination decision issued by the China National Intellectual Property Administration upholding the patent claims on which the patentee initiated the action may be set as a prerequisite for the performance of the judgment items, and arrangements may be made concurrently for the debt interest during the period, so as to reasonably balance the interests of all parties.

2. For a judgment with conditions attached to performance, debt interest for the period of delayed performance may also be adjudicated simultaneously, i.e., after the conditions for performance of the judgment items are fulfilled, interest shall be calculated from the date of service of the effective judgment until the date on which the conditions for performance are fulfilled, at the loan market prime rate announced by the National Interbank Funding Center for the corresponding period (i.e., single interest); if the monetary payment obligation is still not performed after the conditions for performance determined in the judgment are fulfilled, double the debt interest for the period of delayed performance shall be paid.

Civil Judgment of the Supreme People's Court

(2024) Zui Gao Fa Zhi Min Zhong No. 370

Appellant (Defendant at First Instance): Shenzhen Mou Electronic Technology Development Co., Ltd. Domicile: Longgang District, Shenzhen City, Guangdong Province.

Legal Representative: Luo Mou, Executive Director and General Manager of the Company.

Agent ad litem: Yang Qingyu, Attorney at Beijing Gaowo Law Firm.

Appellee (Plaintiff at First Instance): Shenzhen Mou Technology Co., Ltd. Domicile: Longgang District, Shenzhen City, Guangdong Province.

Legal Representative: Zhao Mouqin, Executive Director and General Manager of the Company.

Agent ad litem: Li Longfei, Attorney at Guangdong Guanghe Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Xu Jiaxun, Attorney at Guangdong Guanghe Law Firm.

Defendant at First Instance: Luo Mou, male, domiciled in Jiahe County, Hunan Province.

Agent ad litem: Yang Qingyu, Attorney at Beijing Gaowo Law Firm.

The appellant, Shenzhen Mou Electronic Technology Development Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Shenzhen Mou Electronic Technology Company), appealed to this Court against the civil judgment (2022) Yue 03 Min Chu No. 7208 (hereinafter referred to as the first-instance judgment) rendered by the Intermediate People's Court of Shenzhen City, Guangdong Province (hereinafter referred to as the first-instance court) on September 26, 2023, in the case of dispute over infringement of utility model patent with the appellee, Shenzhen Mou Technology Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Shenzhen Mou Technology Company), and the defendant at first instance, Luo Mou. After accepting the case on March 13, 2024, this Court formed a collegial panel according to law and held a public hearing on July 30, 2024. Yang Qingyu, the common agent ad litem of the appellant Shenzhen Mou Electronic Technology Company and the defendant at first instance Luo Mou, as well as Li Longfei and Xu Jiaxun, the agents ad litem of the appellee Shenzhen Mou Technology Company, appeared in court. The case is now concluded.

Shenzhen Mou Electronic Technology Company appealed with the following requests: 1. Set aside the first-instance judgment and render a new judgment dismissing all claims of Shenzhen Mou Technology Company; 2. The litigation costs of the first and second instances shall be borne by Shenzhen Mou Technology Company. Facts and reasons: (A) The humidifier product manufactured and sold by Shenzhen Mou Electronic Technology Company (hereinafter referred to as the accused infringing product) does not fall within the scope of protection of the utility model patent No. 20212133****.0, titled "Anti-gravity Water Droplet Humidifier" (hereinafter referred to as the patent in question), and does not constitute infringement. Compared with claim 1 of the patent in question, the accused infringing product has different water droplet generating components and humidifying components; compared with claim 5, the technical feature "the upper housing is connected to the lower housing through a column" is different, so the accused infringing product does not fall within the scope of protection of the patent in question. (B) The accused infringing product implements prior art and does not constitute infringement. Shenzhen Mou Electronic Technology Company has submitted prior art evidence with a publication date prior to the filing date of the patent in question. The accused infringing product has exactly the same operating principle and structure as the product design drawing of "Gravity Anti-gravity Humidifier" (hereinafter referred to as the "Anti-gravity Humidifier"), and all technical features that are alleged to fall within the scope of protection of the patent in question are disclosed by this prior art. (C) The rights status of the patent in question is extremely unstable, and Shenzhen Mou Technology Company is not entitled to dispose of the patent in question. Shenzhen Mou Technology Company was sued by a person not involved in the case due to a private lending dispute, and the patent in question, as property of Shenzhen Mou Technology Company, was subject to preservation measures, with the preservation period from January 10, 2023, to January 10, 2026. Pursuant to Article 87 of the Implementing Regulations of the Patent Law of the People's Republic of China (revised in 2010), after a patent is preserved, the relevant procedures concerning the preserved patent application right or patent right shall be suspended, aiming to prevent the patentee from maliciously disposing of the patent right and damaging the rights of the parties in the property preservation case. In a patent infringement lawsuit, the interpretation and explanation of the scope of protection of the patent right are involved, and there is a possibility that the patentee, through malicious and improper interpretation, may damage the rights of the preservation case parties. (D) Multiple defendants accused of infringement have filed invalidation requests with the China National Intellectual Property Administration regarding the patent in question, using the evidence related to the prior art defense in this case, combined with other evidence, to argue that the patent in question lacks novelty and inventiveness. Shenzhen Mou Electronic Technology Company also filed an invalidation request with the China National Intellectual Property Administration within the defense period, and this case should be stayed.

Shenzhen Mou Technology Company argued in defense: (A) The accused infringing product falls within the scope of protection of claims 2, 3, 5-8 of the patent in question and constitutes infringement. (B) The prior art defense raised by Shenzhen Mou Electronic Technology Company is not established. The prior art "Anti-gravity Humidifier" product design drawing only discloses the product appearance and the phenomenon of water droplets in the middle, without disclosing technical features such as the internal structure of the product. (C) Although an invalidation request has been filed against the patent in question, the patent is still valid, which does not affect the trial of the infringement lawsuit in this case. (D) Shenzhen Mou Electronic Technology Company engaged in manufacturing acts and, after repeated warnings from Shenzhen Mou Technology Company and the first-instance judgment, continued to commit the infringing acts, showing obvious malicious intent, and the amount of compensation determined by the first-instance court is relatively low. (E) Shenzhen Mou Technology Company submitted the evaluation report of the patent in question in the first instance, proving that the claims on which the case is based are stable, and there is no need for a stay in this case.

The statements of the defendant at first instance, Luo Mou, are consistent with the appeal opinions of Shenzhen Mou Electronic Technology Company.

Shenzhen Mou Technology Company filed a lawsuit with the first-instance court, which accepted the case on November 16, 2022. Shenzhen Mou Technology Company requested the court to: 1. Order Shenzhen Mou Electronic Technology Company and Luo Mou to immediately cease the acts of infringing the patent in question, and destroy the infringing products in stock and production molds; 2. Order Shenzhen Mou Electronic Technology Company and Luo Mou to jointly and severally compensate Shenzhen Mou Technology Company for economic losses and reasonable expenses for rights protection totaling RMB 200,000; 3. Order Shenzhen Mou Electronic Technology Company and Luo Mou to bear the litigation costs. Facts and reasons: Shenzhen Mou Electronic Technology Company, without authorization, manufactured, offered for sale, and sold the accused infringing product. In July 2022, Shenzhen Mou Technology Company conducted notarized evidence collection of the accused infringing acts. The brand of the accused infringing product sold and offered for sale in the 1688 platform store operated by Shenzhen Mou Electronic Technology Company (hereinafter referred to as the involved 1688 platform store) was "Feng Mou Mou Qi," which is a registered trademark of Shenzhen Mou Electronic Technology Company. In the process of selling the accused infringing product, payments were received through the Alipay account in the personal name of Luo Mou, the legal representative of Shenzhen Mou Electronic Technology Company. Upon comparison, the accused infringing technical solution falls within the scope of protection of the patent in question, and Shenzhen Mou Technology Company requests the court to protect its legitimate rights in accordance with the law.

Shenzhen Mou Electronic Technology Company and Luo Mou jointly argued in defense in the first instance: Shenzhen Mou Electronic Technology Company filed an invalidation request regarding the patent in question and also submitted evidence for a prior art defense, requesting that the judgment be rendered after the issuance of the examination decision on the invalidation request. The accused infringing product manufactured by Shenzhen Mou Electronic Technology Company implements its own patent, and it only became aware of the conflict with the patent in question after Shenzhen Mou Technology Company filed the lawsuit.

The first-instance court found the following facts:

(I) Information Related to the Patent in Question

The patent in question is a utility model patent, with a filing date of June 16, 2021, and an issuance date of February 11, 2022. The patentee is Shenzhen Mou Technology Company. Shenzhen Mou Technology Company has paid the annual patent fee, and the patent in question is in a valid status.

On May 12, 2022, the China National Intellectual Property Administration issued a Utility Model Patent Evaluation Report for the patent in question, stating: Claims 1, 4, and 9 of the patent in question do not meet the conditions for grant of patent rights; no defects were found in claims 2, 3, 5-8 that would prevent the grant of patent rights.

In this case, Shenzhen Mou Technology Company requests protection for claims 2, 3, 5-8 of the patent in question. Claims 1-3 and 5-8 of the patent in question are:

1. An anti-gravity water droplet humidifier, characterized by comprising: a humidifying component, the humidifying component being connected to a mist outlet; a water droplet generating component, the water droplet generating component being connected to a water outlet; a strobe light; wherein the mist outlet and the water outlet are arranged on the same vertical line.

2. The anti-gravity water droplet humidifier according to claim 1, characterized in that the mist outlet is arranged directly above the water outlet.

3. The anti-gravity water droplet humidifier according to claim 2, characterized in that the mist outlet, the humidifying component, the water droplet generating component, and the water outlet are arranged sequentially from top to bottom on the same vertical line.

5. The anti-gravity water droplet humidifier according to claim 1, characterized by further comprising a housing, the housing including an upper housing and a lower housing, the mist outlet, the humidifying component, the water droplet generating component, the water outlet, and the strobe light are arranged in the upper housing, and the upper housing is connected to the lower housing through a column.

6. The anti-gravity water droplet humidifier according to claim 5, characterized by further comprising a water tank, the water tank being connected to the humidifying component and the water droplet generating component through a water pipe and a water pump.

7. The anti-gravity water droplet humidifier according to claim 6, characterized in that the water tank is arranged in the lower housing.

8. The anti-gravity water droplet humidifier according to claim 6, characterized by further comprising a water peak initiator, the water peak initiator having a sharp protrusion, the water peak initiator being arranged below the water outlet, and the water peak initiator being in communication with the water tank.

Paragraph [0018] of the specification of the patent in question states: Compared with the prior art, the utility model has the following beneficial effects: The design is reasonable and easy to use. By arranging the mist outlet of the humidifier component above the water droplet generating component, and in cooperation with the strobe light, an illusion of anti-gravity water droplets rising into the air and turning into mist is created.

(II) Infringement Acts Alleged by Shenzhen Mou Technology Company

Shenzhen Mou Technology Company alleges that Shenzhen Mou Electronic Technology Company and Luo Mou manufactured, offered for sale, and sold the accused infringing product.

Notarial Certificate No. (2022) Shen Xian Zheng Zi No. 40022 issued by Shenzhen Xianxing Notary Office states that the notary office conducted evidence preservation notarization of the process in which the agent of Shenzhen Mou Technology Company received the accused infringing product, and accessed the website "www.1688.com," logged into an account, and viewed the order information for purchasing the accused infringing product and the sales link for the accused infringing product. The notarial certificate records that the sales page of the accused infringing product shows unit prices varying by quantity, with prices of RMB 140, RMB 150, and RMB 179 respectively; over 10 pieces sold in 30 days, with 1 review. Below the product link are buttons for "Select Style and Customize" and "Customize as Needed." The product details column shows that the product number of the accused infringing product is HFJ01, brand "Feng Mou Mou Qi," and major downstream platforms include eBay, Amazon, Wish, AliExpress, independent sites, LAZADA, etc. The store page promotes "Minimum order of 10 pieces," "Customized," and "Laser Engraving." The "Factory Profile" of the involved store records the previously used registered address of Shenzhen Mou Electronic Technology Company. The notarial certificate also includes screenshots of Alibaba Wangwang chat records between the agent of Shenzhen Mou Technology Company and the customer service of Shenzhen Mou Electronic Technology Company, in which Shenzhen Mou Electronic Technology Company indicated it could provide product printing LOGO services.

Shenzhen Mou Technology Company presented the notarized and preserved physical accused infringing products in the first instance, including three accused infringing products, two black and one white. The outer packaging of all three accused infringing products prints "Anti-gravity Water Droplet Humidifier," "Product Model: HJF-01," and "Patent No.: 20223026****.X." Shenzhen Mou Electronic Technology Company confirmed in the first instance that the aforementioned accused infringing products were manufactured, offered for sale, and sold by it.

Both Shenzhen Mou Technology Company and Shenzhen Mou Electronic Technology Company agreed that claims 2, 3, 5-8 asserted by Shenzhen Mou Technology Company can be broken down into the following technical features:

A. An anti-gravity water droplet humidifier, characterized by comprising: a humidifying component, the humidifying component being connected to a mist outlet; B. A water droplet generating component, the water droplet generating component being connected to a water outlet; C. A strobe light; D. Wherein the mist outlet and the water outlet are arranged on the same vertical line; E. The mist outlet is arranged directly above the water outlet; F. The mist outlet, the humidifying component, the water droplet generating component, and the water outlet are arranged sequentially from top to bottom on the same vertical line; G. A housing, the housing including an upper housing and a lower housing, the mist outlet, the humidifying component, the water droplet generating component, the water outlet, and the strobe light are arranged in the upper housing, and the upper housing is connected to the lower housing through a column; H. A water tank, the water tank being connected to the humidifying component and the water droplet generating component through a water pipe and a water pump; I. The water tank is arranged in the lower housing; J. A water peak initiator, the water peak initiator having a sharp protrusion; K. The water peak initiator is arranged below the water outlet, and the water peak initiator is in communication with the water tank. The aforementioned technical features A-D constitute all technical features of claim 1.

The first-instance court disassembled the accused infringing product in court. When the accused infringing product is in normal operation, the mist formed by the product is ejected upward through the mist outlet, and water droplets drip downward from the water outlet directly below the mist outlet. Under the effect of the strobe light, the water droplets appear to move from bottom to top. The disassembled accused infringing product has the following technical features: a. An anti-gravity water droplet humidifier, the humidifying component being connected to the mist outlet; b. A water droplet generating component being connected to the water outlet; c. A strobe light; d. The mist outlet and the water outlet being arranged on the same vertical line; e. The mist outlet being arranged directly above the water outlet; f. The mist outlet, the humidifying component, the water droplet generating component, and the water outlet being arranged sequentially from top to bottom on the same vertical line; g. A housing, the housing including an upper housing and a lower housing, the mist outlet, the humidifying component, the water droplet generating component, the water outlet, and the strobe light being arranged in the upper housing, and the upper housing being connected to the lower housing through a column; h. A water tank, the water tank being connected to the humidifying component and the water droplet generating component through a water pipe and a water pump; i. The water tank being arranged in the lower housing; j. A water peak initiator, the water peak initiator having a sharp protrusion; k. The water peak initiator being arranged below the water outlet, and the water peak initiator being in communication with the water tank.

Shenzhen Mou Technology Company believed that: The accused infringing product includes all technical features of claims 2, 3, 5-8 of the patent in question and falls within the scope of protection of the patent in question. Shenzhen Mou Electronic Technology Company believed that the accused infringing product does not fall within the scope of protection of the patent in question, mainly on the grounds that: The humidifying component and the water droplet generating component of the accused infringing product differ in specific structure and shape from the humidifying component and the water droplet generating component shown in Figure 3 of the specification of the patent in question, so the accused infringing product does not possess technical features A and B; regarding the comparison of other technical features, it agreed with the opinion of Shenzhen Mou Technology Company.

(III) Circumstances of the Invalidation Request and Prior Art Defense Raised by Shenzhen Mou Electronic Technology Company

Shenzhen Mou Electronic Technology Company filed an invalidation request against the patent in question on August 20, 2022.

Shenzhen Mou Electronic Technology Company asserted a prior art defense and submitted the following evidence: 1. A webpage on the SJJS Design Competition website (hereinafter referred to as the Design Competition website) at www.shejijingsai.com/2020/07/519417.html, which on July 5, 2020, displayed product design drawings of "Anti-gravity Humidifier." This evidence only shows the appearance of the product. 2. The NetEase video "Supernatural Phenomenon: Anti-gravity Water Beads, What's the Principle?" at www.163.com/v/video/VKOIPQVIR.html, published on November 26, 2018. This evidence only shows the appearance of anti-gravity water beads. Shenzhen Mou Technology Company believed that the above evidence did not disclose technical features D, E, F, G, H, I, J, K of the patent in question.

(IV) Facts Related to Compensation for Infringement Damages

The reasonable expenses claimed by Shenzhen Mou Technology Company for rights protection totaled RMB 4,730, including notarization fees of RMB 1,000, product purchase fees of RMB 730, and attorney fees shared among related cases filed by Shenzhen Mou Technology Company regarding the patent in question, with RMB 3,000 claimed as attorney fees in this case. Shenzhen Mou Technology Company submitted invoices for notarization fees and attorney fees.

During the first-instance trial, Luo Mou confirmed that payments for products sold through the involved 1688 platform store were credited to his personal Alipay account and had not been settled with Shenzhen Mou Electronic Technology Company.

The first-instance court held that the accused infringing acts occurred after June 1, 2021, and this case should apply the Patent Law of the People's Republic of China as amended in 2020 (hereinafter referred to as the Patent Law). The issues in dispute in this case are: (I) Whether the accused infringing product falls within the scope of protection of the patent in question; (II) Whether the prior art defense asserted by Shenzhen Mou Electronic Technology Company can be established; (III) Whether the amount of compensation claimed by Shenzhen Mou Technology Company is reasonable.

Regarding Disputed Issue 1. Pursuant to Article 64(1) of the Patent Law and Article 7 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Patent Infringement Disputes, Shenzhen Mou Technology Co., Ltd. sought protection for claims 2, 3, and 5-8 of the patent in suit. Each of the above claims constitutes an independent technical solution. Therefore, in conducting the infringement determination, the accused infringing technical solution shall be compared respectively with claims 2, 3, and 5-8 of the patent in suit to determine whether the accused infringing product falls within the scope of protection of each of the above claims. Regarding the dispute on technical comparison, the court of first instance held that: the accused infringing product has a mist outlet through which water mist sprays upward, and a water outlet directly below the mist outlet through which water droplets drip downward. Therefore, the accused infringing product has a humidifying assembly and a water droplet generating assembly corresponding to those features. Claim 1 does not limit the specific shapes and structures of the humidifying assembly and the water droplet generating assembly. The drawings in the specification of the patent in suit are used to explain and illustrate the claims, not to limit the claims. Therefore, Shenzhen Mou Electronic Technology Co., Ltd.'s argument that the humidifying assembly and water droplet generating assembly of the accused infringing product differ in specific structure and shape from those shown in Figure 3 of the specification of the patent in suit cannot stand. The accused infringing product contains all the technical features recited in claims 2, 3, and 5-8 of the patent in suit and falls within the scope of protection of the patent in suit.

Regarding Disputed Issue 2. The evidence submitted by Shenzhen Mou Electronic Technology Co., Ltd. only shows the appearance of the "anti-gravity humidifier" product and the phenomenon of anti-gravity flow of water droplets, but does not disclose the internal technical features of the product. Therefore, Shenzhen Mou Electronic Technology Co., Ltd.'s prior art defense cannot be established.

Regarding Disputed Issue 3. Shenzhen Mou Electronic Technology Co., Ltd., without permission from Shenzhen Mou Technology Co., Ltd., manufactured, offered for sale, and sold products infringing the patent in suit for profit-making purposes. It shall bear civil liability for ceasing the infringement, destroying the infringing products in inventory, and compensating for losses. Luo used a personal account to collect payments for the store on the 1688 platform involved in this case and did not settle accounts with Shenzhen Mou Electronic Technology Co., Ltd., thus constituting joint infringement with Shenzhen Mou Electronic Technology Co., Ltd. Shenzhen Mou Technology Co., Ltd. did not provide evidence to prove that the accused infringing product involved dedicated equipment molds, so the relevant claims are not supported.

Regarding the amount of compensation. Since the losses of Shenzhen Mou Technology Co., Ltd. and the profits of Shenzhen Mou Electronic Technology Co., Ltd. are both difficult to determine, and Shenzhen Mou Technology Co., Ltd. did not submit evidence to prove its patent license fees, and Shenzhen Mou Technology Co., Ltd. requested the court to determine the amount of compensation at its discretion. The court of first instance, taking into account the type of patent right involved, the nature and circumstances of the infringing act, reasonable expenses for rights protection, and other factors, determined at its discretion that Shenzhen Mou Electronic Technology Co., Ltd. and Luo shall jointly and severally compensate Shenzhen Mou Technology Co., Ltd. for economic losses and reasonable expenses for rights protection totaling RMB 150,000.

The court of first instance, in accordance with Article 2(3), Article 11(1), Article 64(1), Article 71 of the Patent Law of the PRC, Articles 1 and 7 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Patent Infringement Disputes, and Article 67 of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC as amended in 2021, rendered the following judgment: "1. The defendants, Shenzhen Mou Electronic Technology Development Co., Ltd. and Luo, shall immediately cease infringing the plaintiff's patent right No. 20212133****.0 and destroy the infringing products in inventory; 2. The defendants, Shenzhen Mou Electronic Technology Development Co., Ltd. and Luo, shall, within ten days from the effective date of this judgment, jointly and severally compensate the plaintiff, Shenzhen Mou Technology Co., Ltd., for economic losses and reasonable expenses for rights protection totaling RMB 150,000; 3. All other claims of the plaintiff, Shenzhen Mou Technology Co., Ltd., are dismissed. If the obligation to pay money is not fulfilled within the period specified in this judgment, interest on the debt for the period of delayed performance shall be doubled in accordance with Article 260 of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC. The case acceptance fee of RMB 4,300 shall be borne by the defendants, Shenzhen Mou Electronic Technology Development Co., Ltd. and Luo."

During the second instance of this court, Shenzhen Mou Electronic Technology Co., Ltd. and Luo, in order to prove their claims, submitted the following new evidence to this court:

First set of evidence: The "Notice of Commencement of Preservation Procedures" issued by the China National Intellectual Property Administration (CNIPA) regarding the patent in suit, three "Notices of Acceptance of Invalidation Requests" (Invalidation requester: Shenzhen Mou Electronic Technology Co., Ltd., case number 5W129316; invalidation requester: third party Shenzhen Mou Investment Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Mou Investment Company), case number 5W132929; invalidation requester: third party Dongguan Mou Electronic Technology Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Dongguan Mou Electronic Technology Company), case number 5W134452), and relevant evidence submitted by Shenzhen Mou Electronic Technology Co., Ltd., Mou Investment Company, and Dongguan Mou Electronic Technology Company to the CNIPA in the patent invalidation administrative procedures. Purportedly to prove that the CNIPA has accepted the invalidation requests filed by Shenzhen Mou Electronic Technology Co., Ltd., Mou Investment Company, and Dongguan Mou Electronic Technology Company against the patent in suit, and that the rights status of the patent in suit is extremely unstable. Furthermore, the CNIPA has already taken property preservation measures against the patent in suit, and Shenzhen Mou Technology Co., Ltd. has no right to dispose of the patent in suit, so its claims should not be supported.

Second set of evidence: Delivery order details issued by third party Dongguan Mou Electronic Technology Company to Shenzhen Mou Electronic Technology Co., Ltd., sales records of Shenzhen Mou Electronic Technology Co., Ltd.'s store on the 1688 platform involved in this case, and a cost breakdown table for the manufacture of the accused infringing product prepared by Dongguan Mou Electronic Technology Company. Purportedly to prove: 1. The accused infringing products were all manufactured by Dongguan Mou Electronic Technology Company and sold by Shenzhen Mou Electronic Technology Co., Ltd. through the 1688 platform store and other channels; the manufacturing cost of the accused infringing product is RMB 42.635, with a shipping cost of RMB 10 per unit; the unit price of the accused infringing product sold offline by Shenzhen Mou Electronic Technology Co., Ltd. is RMB 45, resulting in a profit of RMB 2.365 per unit after deducting manufacturing costs; the unit price of the accused infringing product sold on the 1688 platform store is RMB 57, resulting in a profit of RMB 4.365 per unit after deducting manufacturing costs and shipping fees; 2. Shenzhen Mou Technology Co., Ltd. obtained compensation of RMB 80,000 in case (2022) Yue 73 Zhi Min Chu No. 1603 filed in the Guangzhou Intellectual Property Court against Dongguan Mou Electronic Technology Company as the defendant, and the RMB 150,000 compensation adjudged in the first instance of this case duplicates the compensation in the above case.

Shenzhen Mou Technology Co., Ltd.'s opinion on the evidence: It acknowledges the authenticity and legality of the first set of evidence but does not acknowledge its relevance and the purpose of proof, as the invalidation request for the patent in suit is still under review and the patent remains valid. It does not acknowledge the second set of evidence, arguing that Dongguan Mou Electronic Technology Company and Shenzhen Mou Electronic Technology Co., Ltd. are affiliated companies controlled by Luo, and the evidence unilaterally prepared by Dongguan Mou Electronic Technology Company lacks corroboration and is not probative.

Regarding the evidence submitted by Shenzhen Mou Electronic Technology Co., Ltd. and Luo, this court's opinion on certification is as follows: Shenzhen Mou Technology Co., Ltd. has no objection to the authenticity of the first set of evidence, and this court confirms its authenticity. The second set of evidence is not admitted, as Shenzhen Mou Electronic Technology Co., Ltd. did not provide the originals for verification, and Dongguan Mou Electronic Technology Company and Shenzhen Mou Electronic Technology Co., Ltd. are affiliated companies. The cost breakdown table issued by Dongguan Mou Electronic Technology Company was unilaterally prepared without corroborating evidence. Regarding the issue of duplicate compensation raised by Shenzhen Mou Electronic Technology Co., Ltd. and Luo, this court will determine the accused infringing products corresponding to the compensation in this case based on Shenzhen Mou Technology Co., Ltd.'s claim for damages.

Shenzhen Mou Technology Co., Ltd., to prove its claims, submitted two new pieces of evidence to this court: 1. Screenshots of Alibaba Wangwang chat records, purportedly to prove that Shenzhen Mou Electronic Technology Co., Ltd. continued to sell the accused infringing product on the 1688 platform store after the first-instance judgment was rendered. 2. Screenshots of the sales page of the accused infringing product on the 1688 platform store, certified by trusted timestamp, purportedly to prove that as of March 19, 2024, Shenzhen Mou Electronic Technology Co., Ltd. was still engaging in acts infringing the patent in suit.

Shenzhen Mou Electronic Technology Co., Ltd. and Luo's opinion on the evidence: They acknowledge the authenticity of the above evidence but do not acknowledge its relevance, arguing that the products shown in the screenshots do not reveal their internal structure and cannot be proven to be infringing products.

Regarding the evidence submitted by Shenzhen Mou Technology Co., Ltd., this court's opinion on certification is as follows: Since Shenzhen Mou Electronic Technology Co., Ltd. and Luo did not raise objections to the authenticity of this evidence, this court confirms its authenticity.

During the second instance, this court requested Shenzhen Mou Technology Co., Ltd. to disclose the circumstances of related cases nationwide and the status of preservation measures taken against the patent in suit. Shenzhen Mou Technology Co., Ltd. submitted to this court the "Information Table of Related Cases", the civil judgment (2023) Yue 03 Min Chu No. 4107 of the court of first instance, the civil mediation document (2022) Yue 0309 Min Chu No. 17187 (hereinafter referred to as Case No. 17187) of the Longhua District People's Court of Shenzhen, Guangdong Province (hereinafter referred to as Longhua District People's Court), and the domestic payment receipt for the transfer of RMB 300,000 by third party Shenzhen Mou Internet Technology Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Shenzhen Mou Internet Company) to Shenzhen Mou Technology Co., Ltd. Shenzhen Mou Electronic Technology Co., Ltd. and Luo did not object to the above evidence.

The facts found by the court of first instance are basically true, and this court confirms them.

Based on the evidence on file, this court further finds the following facts related to the disputed issues:

(1) Facts related to the patent in suit

Shenzhen Mou Electronic Technology Co., Ltd., as well as third parties Mou Investment Company and Dongguan Mou Electronic Technology Company, respectively filed invalidation requests against the patent in suit with the CNIPA. Details are as follows:

On August 20, 2022, Shenzhen Mou Electronic Technology Co., Ltd. filed an invalidation request against the patent in suit with the CNIPA, requesting that claims 1-7 and 9 of the patent in suit be declared invalid. The CNIPA accepted it on August 29, 2022, and conducted an oral hearing on February 2, 2023.

On June 28, 2023, third party Mou Investment Company filed an invalidation request against the patent in suit with the CNIPA. In the appendix to the invalidation request, Mou Investment Company argued that claims 1-9 of the patent in suit lacked inventiveness and requested that all claims of the patent in suit be declared invalid. Regarding the additional technical features of claim 8, Mou Investment Company submitted to the CNIPA Chinese utility model patent with authorization announcement number CN20274****U (hereinafter referred to as the 529 patent), arguing that this evidence discloses that the lower housing of the water droplet humidifier is provided with a recess for receiving water droplets falling from the upper housing, and the recess is connected to the water tank. A person of ordinary skill in the art would readily conceive of the additional technical features of claim 8. Since the claim 6 from which it depends lacks inventiveness, claim 8 also lacks inventiveness.

On October 30, 2023, third party Dongguan Mou Electronic Technology Company filed an invalidation request against the patent in suit with the CNIPA. In the appendix to the invalidation request, Dongguan Mou Electronic Technology Company argued that claims 1-9 of the patent in suit lacked inventiveness and requested that all claims of the patent in suit be declared invalid. Regarding the additional technical features of claim 8, Dongguan Mou Electronic Technology Company submitted the 529 patent and a Netease video titled "Anti-Gravity Water Droplet Clock – What's the principle?" certified by trusted timestamp. The video was published on February 17, 2021, and multiple comments below the video were published in February or April 2021. The video shows that the bottom of the anti-gravity water droplet clock is provided with a sharply protruding water-starting peak, which is located below the water outlet. In the appendix to the invalidation request, Dongguan Mou Electronic Technology Company stated: 1. The 529 patent discloses that the lower housing of the water droplet humidifier is provided with a recess for receiving water droplets falling from the upper housing, and the recess is connected to the water tank. Based on the above disclosure, a person of ordinary skill in the art would readily conceive of the additional technical features of claim 8. Since the claim 6 from which it depends lacks inventiveness, claim 8 also lacks inventiveness. 2. The "Anti-Gravity Water Droplet Clock – What's the principle?" video discloses that a water-starting peak is provided on the lower housing, the water-starting peak has a sharp protrusion, and the water-starting peak is located below the water outlet. The video shows that falling water droplets pass through the water-starting peak and then flow into the water tank, so the water-starting peak must be connected to the water tank. Therefore, the above video, or the video combined with common general knowledge, discloses the additional technical features of claim 8.

The "Information Table of Related Cases" submitted by Shenzhen Mou Technology Co., Ltd. shows that third parties Dongguan Hong Mou Electronic Technology Co., Ltd., San Mou Technology (Shenzhen) Co., Ltd., and Huizhou Di Mou Electronic Technology Co., Ltd. also separately filed invalidation requests against the patent in suit with the CNIPA.

Third party Shenzhen Mou Internet Company filed a civil action for private lending dispute against Shenzhen Mou Technology Co., Ltd. in the Longhua District People's Court, which accepted the case on December 5, 2022, under case number 17187. In Case No. 17187, Shenzhen Mou Internet Company requested that Shenzhen Mou Technology Co., Ltd. repay a loan of RMB 300,000. Upon application by Shenzhen Mou Internet Company, the Longhua District People's Court issued a ruling (2022) Yue 0309 Zhi Bao 7002, ruling to take preservation measures against the patent in suit. To enforce the above ruling, the CNIPA decided "to assist in the execution of property preservation for this patent from January 10, 2023 to January 10, 2026." Shenzhen Mou Internet Company and Shenzhen Mou Technology Co., Ltd. reached a settlement in the private lending dispute, and the Longhua District People's Court issued a civil mediation document (2022) Yue 0309 Min Chu No. 17187 on July 7, 2023, which mainly provided that: Shenzhen Mou Technology Co., Ltd. shall pay RMB 300,000 to Shenzhen Mou Internet Company in three installments by bank transfer before August 1, 2026; the first installment of RMB 100,000 shall be paid before August 1, 2024; the second installment of RMB 100,000 shall be paid before August 1, 2025; the third installment of RMB 100,000 shall be paid before August 1, 2026; Shenzhen Mou Internet Company shall, within five working days after receiving all payments, apply to the Longhua District People's Court for the release of the property preservation measures.

The domestic payment receipt for the transfer of RMB 300,000 by Shenzhen Mou Internet Company to Shenzhen Mou Technology Co., Ltd. states that the transfer was made on July 8, 2022, for the purpose of a loan.

Due to the property preservation measures taken against the patent in suit in Case No. 17187, the relevant patent invalidation administrative procedures initiated against the patent in suit have all been suspended by the CNIPA.

(2) Facts related to the technical features of the accused infringing product and the prior art defense

During the second instance, this court organized both parties to examine the relevant technical features of the accused infringing product. Upon disassembling the accused infringing product, it can be observed that the housing of the accused infringing product includes an upper housing and a lower housing, connected by two symmetrical columns. Observing the internal structure of the upper housing, from top to bottom, there are sequentially a mist outlet, a humidifying device, a water droplet generating device, a water outlet, a water-starting peak, and a water pump. The mist outlet, humidifying device, water droplet generating device, and water outlet are substantially in the same vertical direction. The humidifying device and the water droplet generating device are fixed together by screws. The upper layer of the humidifying device is a circular structure with a center hole, the middle layer is a small circular component connecting wires, and the lower layer is a square component connecting to the water droplet generating device. On both sides of the square component, there are water pipes connecting to other components. Specifically, one water pipe passes through the column on the same side to connect to the water pump, and the other water pipe bends to connect to the water droplet generating device. After removing the screws of the water droplet generating device, it can be seen that the water droplet generating device includes a generator component connected to the humidifying device, a rubber ring, and a recessed accommodating cavity. The bottom of the accommodating cavity communicates with the water outlet. Three strobe lights are evenly arranged around the bottom of the water outlet. Directly below the water outlet, there is a sharply protruding water-starting peak, which communicates with the water tank. The water tank is set in the lower housing, and the water tank is connected to the humidifying device and the water droplet generating device through water pipes connected to the water pump.

The prior art defense evidence submitted by Shenzhen Mou Electronic Technology Co., Ltd. at first instance includes: a design drawing and design description of the "anti-gravity humidifier" product displayed on the design competition website on July 5, 2020, in the "Lu Xun Academy of Fine Arts 2020 Graduation Season Industrial Design College Graduation Works". The "Design Description" states: This Gravity humidifier, based on the phenomenon of visual illusion, brings a unique visual interaction experience to people. ... The water column is divided into three modes: visual upward flow, suspension, and descent. As for the principle of water droplet suspension and reverse flow in the structure, it uses the flash frequency of strobe lights and the effect of visual persistence, observing the water flow state through light refraction. Photographing water droplets falling at the same visual interval, if the flash frequency of the strobe lights and the time interval of water droplet falling maintain a uniform frequency, the special effect of water droplet suspension seen by the human eye can be obtained.

Shenzhen Mou Technology Co., Ltd. argued that the above evidence does not disclose the internal technical features of the "anti-gravity humidifier". No technical features such as a humidifying assembly, water droplet generating assembly, or strobe lights were observed or recorded. Moreover, the water outlet and mist outlet are clearly not in the same vertical line, and they cannot form a one-to-one correspondence with the technical solution of the patent in suit.

(3) Facts related to infringement compensation

Shenzhen Mou Technology Co., Ltd. specified that the period of alleged infringement in this case is from July 7, 2022 (the date of notarized purchase of the accused infringing product) to May 13, 2024 (the latest date of sale of the accused infringing product as evidenced by the evidence on file). The scope of infringing products is the accused infringing product manufactured by Shenzhen Mou Electronic Technology Co., Ltd. during the aforementioned period and offered for sale and sold on the 1688 platform store involved in this case. Shenzhen Mou Electronic Technology Co., Ltd. argued that this case can only address the alleged infringing acts occurring before the conclusion of the first-instance court debate, i.e., before May 30, 2023.

In the case (2023) Yue 03 Min Chu No. 4107 accepted by the court of first instance, Shenzhen Mou Technology Co., Ltd. v. Mou Investment Company and Shenzhen Mou Electronic Technology Co., Ltd. — dispute over infringement of utility model patent, Shenzhen Mou Technology Co., Ltd. requested protection for claims 5-8 of the patent in suit. Mou Investment Company admitted that the profit margin of the accused infringing product was 15%-30%. The court of first instance rendered a judgment on November 13, 2023, finding that Mou Investment Company and Shenzhen Mou Electronic Technology Co., Ltd. constituted joint infringement. Since the manufacturing act had already been adjudicated and compensated in another case (i.e., the first instance of this case), the amount of damages in that case was calculated only based on the sales volume of the infringing products of Mou Investment Company. The court ordered Mou Investment Company and Shenzhen Mou Electronic Technology Co., Ltd. to cease infringement and jointly and severally compensate Shenzhen Mou Technology Co., Ltd. for economic losses and reasonable expenses in the amount of 20,000 yuan. Mou Investment Company and Shenzhen Mou Electronic Technology Co., Ltd. appealed to the Guangdong High People's Court. The Guangdong High People's Court rendered a civil judgment (2024) Yue Zhi Min Zhong No. 283 on August 19, 2024, dismissing the appeal and affirming the original judgment. In this case, Shenzhen Mou Technology Co., Ltd. argued that the profit margin of the infringing product in this case should be determined by reference to the profit margin of the infringing product admitted by Mou Investment Company in the aforementioned case.

At the request of this court, Shenzhen Mou Technology Co., Ltd. disclosed a total of 30 related cases involving the patent in suit. During the second instance, Shenzhen Mou Technology Co., Ltd. clarified that it would allocate the 30,000 yuan in attorney's fees incurred to the 30 related cases, claiming 1,000 yuan in attorney's fees per case. In this case, it also claimed 500 yuan in travel expenses, and the notarization fee was determined to be 1,000 yuan based on the invoice provided by Shenzhen Mou Technology Co., Ltd.

Shenzhen Mou Technology Co., Ltd. was established on December 30, 2019, with a business scope including research and development of household appliances, sales of electronic products, sales of smart home consumption equipment, etc. This court finds ex officio that, according to the query results on the official website of the China National Intellectual Property Administration, Shenzhen Mou Technology Co., Ltd. currently has 17 valid patents, including 1 invention, 12 utility models, and 4 design patents. Most of the patents relate to humidifiers and their components.

Shenzhen Mou Electronic Technology Co., Ltd. was established on May 27, 2020, with a legal representative of Luo, and its business scope includes wholesale and retail of electronic products; wholesale and retail of electronic products and electronic components; operation of e-commerce, etc.

Mou Investment Company was established on May 4, 2010, with a legal representative of Guo Mouqian, and its business scope includes sales of electronic products, household appliances, digital products, etc. The shareholders include Luo, Liu, and Li, with Luo holding 35% equity and serving as the company's supervisor. Luo and Guo Mouqian are husband and wife.

Dongguan Mou Electronic Technology Co., Ltd. was established on April 21, 2021, with the legal representative originally being Luo, changed to Liu on August 20, 2023. The company's business scope includes research and development, production, processing, and sales of electronic products, etc.

This court holds: Based on the facts found and the allegations and defenses of both parties, the issues in dispute at the second instance stage are: (1) whether the accused infringing technical solution falls within the scope of protection of the patent in suit; (2) whether the prior art defense can be established; (3) how to determine the liability for infringement; (4) how to enforce the judgment in this case.

(I) Regarding the issue of whether the accused infringing technical solution falls within the scope of protection of the patent in suit.

Article 64, paragraph 1 of the Patent Law provides: "The scope of protection of an invention or utility model patent shall be determined by the content of the claims. The description and drawings may be used to interpret the content of the claims." Article 7 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Patent Infringement Dispute Cases provides: "When determining whether the accused infringing technical solution falls within the scope of protection of the patent, the people's court shall examine all the technical features recorded in the claims asserted by the right holder. If the accused infringing technical solution contains technical features that are identical or equivalent to all the technical features recorded in the claims, the people's court shall find that it falls within the scope of protection of the patent. If, compared with all the technical features recorded in the claims, the accused infringing technical solution lacks one or more technical features recorded in the claims, or has one or more technical features that are neither identical nor equivalent, the people's court shall find that it does not fall within the scope of protection of the patent."

Shenzhen Mou Technology Co., Ltd. filed this lawsuit based on claims 2, 3, and 5-8 of the patent in suit. Shenzhen Mou Electronic Technology Co., Ltd. argued that the accused infringing product lacks the technical features of "humidifying assembly" and "water droplet generating assembly" recorded in claim 1 of the patent in suit, as well as the technical feature of "the upper shell and the lower shell are connected by columns" recorded in claim 5; it acknowledged that the accused infringing technical solution possesses the other technical features recorded in claims 2, 3, and 5-8 of the patent in suit. Shenzhen Mou Technology Co., Ltd. argued that there are humidifying assemblies and water droplet generating assemblies in the upper shell of the accused infringing product. Claim 5 of the patent in suit does not limit whether the connection between the upper shell and the lower shell by columns is separable or integrally formed, and the scheme in which the upper shell and the lower shell of the accused infringing product are connected by columns on the left and right sides falls within the scope of protection of the patent.

This court holds: Regarding technical dispute point 1, "humidifying assembly" and "water droplet generating assembly." Shenzhen Mou Electronic Technology Co., Ltd. did not object to the fact that the accused infringing product has a humidifying device and a water droplet generating device, and can achieve the technical effects of mist output from the mist outlet and water output from the water outlet. It only argued that its humidifying device and water droplet generating device are an integral structure, and there is no feature of being composed of multiple structural components. This court finds that the accused infringing product has a humidifying device and a water droplet generating device. The upper layer of the humidifying device is a circular structure with a center hole, the middle layer is a small circular component connecting to wires, and the lower layer is a square component connecting to the water droplet generating device. On both sides of the square component, water pipes are respectively connected to other components; specifically, one water pipe passes through the column on the same side to connect with the water pump, and the other water pipe bends and connects to the water droplet generating device. The water droplet generating device includes a generator component connected to the humidifying device, a rubber ring, and a sunken accommodating cavity, the bottom of which communicates with the water outlet. Claim 1 of the patent in suit does not limit the specific structure of the "humidifying assembly" and "water droplet generating assembly." The humidifying device and water droplet generating device of the accused infringing product are no different from the technical features of "humidifying assembly" and "water droplet generating assembly" recorded in claim 1 of the patent in suit. Therefore, Shenzhen Mou Electronic Technology Co., Ltd.'s contention regarding technical dispute point 1 cannot be established.

Regarding technical dispute point 2, "the upper shell and the lower shell are connected by columns." In the accused infringing product, the water tank in the lower shell is connected to the humidifying device and the water droplet generating device via a water pipe connected to a water pump, and the water pipe connected to the water pump runs from top to bottom through one column. The manner in which the upper shell and the lower shell of the accused infringing product are connected by columns falls within the scope of protection of the patent in suit. Therefore, Shenzhen Mou Electronic Technology Co., Ltd.'s appeal argument cannot be established, and this court does not support it.

Given that Shenzhen Mou Electronic Technology Co., Ltd. has not objected to the other technical features of the accused infringing product that correspond to claims 2, 3, and 5-8 of the patent in suit, this court will not elaborate on the comparison of other features.

In summary, the accused infringing technical solution contains all the technical features recorded in claims 2, 3, and 5-8 of the patent in suit and falls within the scope of protection of the patent in suit. The first instance judgment's finding on this point is proper, and this court affirms it.

(II) Regarding the issue of whether the prior art defense can be established.

Article 22, paragraph 5 of the Patent Law provides: "For the purposes of this Law, the term 'existing technology' means technology that is known to the public both at home and abroad before the date of filing." Article 67 provides: "In a patent infringement dispute, if the alleged infringer has evidence to prove that the technology or design it implements is existing technology or existing design, it shall not be deemed to have infringed the patent right." Article 14, paragraph 1 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Patent Infringement Dispute Cases provides: "If all the technical features that are alleged to fall within the scope of protection of the patent are identical or have no substantial difference from the corresponding technical features in a prior art solution, the people's court shall find that the technology implemented by the alleged infringer is existing technology as defined in Article 62 of the Patent Law."

In this case, the prior art evidence submitted by Shenzhen Mou Electronic Technology Co., Ltd. is the product design drawing and design description of the "anti-gravity humidifier," which was disclosed in July 2020, earlier than the filing date of the patent in suit, June 16, 2021, and can be used as prior art. This court has previously found that the accused infringing technical solution possesses all the technical features of claims 2, 3, and 5-8 of the patent in suit. Pursuant to the above provisions, whether the prior art defense in this case is established requires separate examination of whether all the technical features alleged to fall within the scope of protection of claims 2, 3, 5, 6, 7, and 8 are identical or have no substantial difference from the corresponding technical features in the prior art. During the second instance, this court organized the parties to compare the accused infringing technical solution with the prior art solution. In response to the parties' arguments, this court provides the following analysis:

1. Regarding the identification of the contents disclosed in the prior art. The product design drawing of the "anti-gravity humidifier" includes design drawings and textual descriptions, disclosing a water flow column visible in the middle, which operates in three modes: upward flow, suspension, and downward flow. A strobe light is arranged around the water outlet, utilizing the strobe effect and visual persistence to observe the water flow state through light refraction, achieving a visual effect of suspended and reverse-flowing water droplets. From the product design drawing, it can be seen that the shell includes an upper shell and a lower shell; the mist outlet, water outlet, and strobe light are provided on the upper shell; the upper shell and the lower shell are connected by a circular member. The mist outlet is located directly above the water outlet, from which it can be inferred that the mist outlet and the water outlet are on the same vertical line. Furthermore, since the work is a humidifier, with mist expelled from the top to humidify the air, it necessarily has a humidifying assembly. To allow the atomized mist to enter the air for humidification, the humidifying assembly must be connected to the mist outlet. Since the humidifier has water droplets flowing downward, it can be directly and unequivocally determined that the existing design has a water droplet generator to form falling water droplets from the top of the humidifier; the water droplets flowing out of the water droplet generating assembly must exit through the water outlet, so the water droplet generating assembly must be connected to the water outlet.

2. Regarding all the technical features alleged to fall within the scope of protection of claim 2 of the patent in suit. The contents identified above disclose all the technical features alleged to fall within the scope of protection of claim 1. Claim 2 depends on claim 1, with the additional technical feature being "the mist outlet is provided directly above the water outlet." From the product design drawing of the "anti-gravity humidifier," it can be seen that the mist outlet is located directly above the water outlet, which is identical to the additional technical feature alleged to fall within the scope of protection of claim 2. Thus, the prior art discloses all the technical features alleged to fall within the scope of protection of claim 2.

3. Regarding all the technical features alleged to fall within the scope of protection of claim 3 of the patent in suit. Claim 3 depends on claim 2, with the additional technical feature being "the mist outlet, the humidifying assembly, the water droplet generating assembly, and the water outlet are arranged sequentially from top to bottom on the same vertical line." Although the product design drawing of the "anti-gravity humidifier" discloses that the mist outlet and the water outlet are arranged from top to bottom on the same vertical line, since the humidifying assembly and the water droplet generating assembly are internal structures, it cannot be directly and unequivocally determined from the product design drawing and textual description that the mist outlet, humidifying assembly, water droplet generating assembly, and water outlet are on the same vertical line. The corresponding technical features in the prior art are not identical to the above-mentioned technical features alleged to fall within the scope of claim 3. However, based on the working principle of the "anti-gravity humidifier," there is no substantial difference between arranging the mist outlet, humidifying assembly, water droplet generating assembly, and water outlet from top to bottom and arranging them on the same vertical line. Moreover, the patent in suit does not describe any specific technical effect of "arranged sequentially from top to bottom on the same vertical line." Therefore, the corresponding technical features in the prior art are identical or have no substantial difference from all the technical features alleged to fall within the scope of protection of claim 3.

4. Regarding all the technical features alleged to fall within the scope of protection of claim 5 of the patent in suit. Claim 5 depends on claim 1, with the additional technical feature being "further comprising a housing, the housing including an upper shell and a lower shell, the mist outlet, the humidifying assembly, the water droplet generating assembly, the water outlet, and the strobe light are provided on the upper shell, and the upper shell and the lower shell are connected by columns." The product design drawing of the "anti-gravity humidifier" discloses a humidifier including a housing, the housing including an upper shell and a lower shell, with the mist outlet, water outlet, and strobe light provided on the upper shell, and the upper shell and the lower shell are connected by a circular member. From the working principle of the "anti-gravity humidifier," it can be inferred that the mist outlet and the water outlet must be connected to the humidifying assembly and the water droplet generating assembly, respectively, so the humidifying assembly and the water droplet generating assembly must be located in the upper shell. As for the connection between the upper shell and the lower shell, there is no substantial difference between using column connection or circular member connection. The corresponding technical features in the prior art are identical or have no substantial difference from all the technical features alleged to fall within the scope of protection of claim 5.

5. Regarding all the technical features alleged to fall within the scope of protection of claim 6 of the patent in suit. Claim 6 depends on claim 5, with the additional technical feature being "further comprising a water tank, the water tank is connected to the humidifying assembly and the water droplet generating assembly via water pipes and a water pump." The product design drawing of the "anti-gravity humidifier" does not directly disclose the additional technical feature alleged to fall within the scope of claim 6. However, based on the working state of the "anti-gravity humidifier," it can be unequivocally concluded that the humidifier must have a water tank, as well as a water pump and water pipes to draw water from the water tank to the upper water outlet. Therefore, the corresponding technical features in the prior art are identical or have no substantial difference from all the technical features alleged to fall within the scope of protection of claim 6.

6. Regarding all the technical features alleged to fall within the scope of protection of claim 7 of the patent in suit. Claim 7 depends on claim 6, with the additional technical feature being "the water tank is provided in the lower shell." Although the product design drawing does not directly disclose the additional technical feature alleged to fall within the scope of claim 7, based on the overall structure and usage state of the "anti-gravity humidifier," it can be concluded that it has a water tank located in the lower shell. Therefore, the corresponding technical features in the prior art are identical or have no substantial difference from all the technical features alleged to fall within the scope of protection of claim 7.

In summary, Shenzhen Mou Electronic Technology Co., Ltd.'s prior art defense concerning claims 2, 3, 5, 6, and 7 is established. However, the product design drawing of the "anti-gravity humidifier" does not disclose the additional technical feature "water peak" alleged to fall within the scope of protection of claim 8 of the patent in suit. Based on the existing evidence, Shenzhen Mou Electronic Technology Co., Ltd.'s prior art defense concerning claim 8 cannot be established.

(III) Regarding the issue of how to determine the liability for infringement in this case.

Article 11, paragraph 1 of the Patent Law provides: "After the grant of an invention or utility model patent, except as otherwise provided by this Law, no entity or individual may, without the permission of the patentee, exploit the patent, i.e., may not manufacture, use, offer to sell, sell, or import the patented product, or use the patented method, or use, offer to sell, sell, or import a product directly obtained by the patented method, for production or business purposes." Pursuant to Article 179, paragraph 1 of the Civil Code of the People's Republic of China, the methods of bearing civil liability include cessation of infringement, compensation for losses, etc. As stated above, Shenzhen Mou Electronic Technology Co., Ltd.'s acts of manufacturing, offering to sell, and selling the accused infringing product fall within the scope of protection of claim 8 of the patent in suit, and its prior art defense for the technical solution alleged to fall within the scope of protection of claim 8 cannot be established. Therefore, it should be found to have infringed the patent in suit. Consistent with Shenzhen Mou Technology Co., Ltd.'s claims, Shenzhen Mou Electronic Technology Co., Ltd. and Luo shall cease the acts of manufacturing, offering to sell, and selling the accused infringing product, destroy the infringing products in stock, and bear civil liability for compensating Shenzhen Mou Technology Co., Ltd. for its losses.

Article 71, paragraphs 1, 2, and 3 of the Patent Law provide: "The amount of damages for patent infringement shall be determined according to the actual losses suffered by the right holder due to the infringement or the profits gained by the infringer due to the infringement. If it is difficult to determine the losses of the right holder or the profits of the infringer, the amount may be determined reasonably by reference to the multiple of the patent license fee. If the infringement is intentional and the circumstances are serious, the amount of damages may be determined at not less than one time but not more than five times the amount determined according to the above methods. If it is difficult to determine the losses of the right holder, the profits of the infringer, and the patent license fee, the people's court may determine the amount of damages within the range of not less than 30,000 yuan but not more than 5,000,000 yuan based on factors such as the type of the patent right and the nature and circumstances of the infringement. The amount of damages shall also include the reasonable expenses incurred by the right holder to stop the infringement."

Regarding the issue of how to determine the amount of damages. During the second instance, Shenzhen Mou Technology Co., Ltd. further clarified the infringing product to which its damages claim pertains. Since Shenzhen Mou Electronic Technology Co., Ltd. did not agree to have the court of second instance adjudicate the accused infringing acts occurring after the conclusion of the oral argument at the first instance, this court will only determine the amount of damages for the accused infringing products that were manufactured by Shenzhen Mou Electronic Technology Co., Ltd. before the conclusion of the oral argument at the first instance, i.e., before May 30, 2023, and sold through the relevant 1688 platform store. For the accused infringing acts occurring thereafter, Shenzhen Mou Technology Co., Ltd. may assert its rights separately.

In determining the amount of compensation in this case, this Court considered the following factors: 1. The nature of the infringing act. In this case, the accused infringing product was manufactured by Shenzhen [a certain] Electronic Technology Co., Ltd. and was offered for sale and sold on the 1688 platform store operated by it. 2. The quantity of infringing products. Based on the evidence on file, from July 7, 2022, the date of notarized purchase of the accused infringing product by Shenzhen [a certain] Technology Co., Ltd., to May 30, 2023, Shenzhen [a certain] Electronic Technology Co., Ltd. continuously infringed the patent-in-suit for a total of 11 months. Shenzhen [a certain] Electronic Technology Co., Ltd. claimed that it sold only a very small number of infringing products on its 1688 platform store, but did not provide evidence of actual sales volume. Therefore, this Court, with reference to the sales volume of the store at the time of evidence collection by Shenzhen [a certain] Technology Co., Ltd., being "10+ transactions in 30 days" as displayed on the notarized evidence collection page, determined the total sales volume during the period of infringement. 3. The sales price and reasonable profit of the infringing products. According to the evidence provided by Shenzhen [a certain] Technology Co., Ltd., the selling prices of the accused infringing products on the 1688 platform store of Shenzhen [a certain] Electronic Technology Co., Ltd. varied according to the order quantity, being 140 yuan, 150 yuan, and 179 yuan, with an average price of approximately 156 yuan. Since none of the parties provided a reasonable profit margin for the accused infringing products, this Court, with reference to the average profit margin of the processing industry and the profit margin of the infringing product admitted by [a certain] Investment Company, reasonably determined the profit on the infringing products. In addition, the circumstances of the prior art defense in this case should also be considered, and the difference between the patent-in-suit and the prior art and its contribution rate to the entire accused infringing product should be reasonably determined. Taking the above factors into comprehensive consideration, this Court determines the amount of compensation in this case to be 7,500 yuan.

In accordance with Article 71 of the Patent Law, the amount of compensation shall also include the reasonable expenses incurred by the right holder to stop the infringing act. In this case, Shenzhen [a certain] Technology Co., Ltd. claimed attorney's fees of 1,000 yuan, travel expenses of 500 yuan, and notarization fees of 1,000 yuan, totaling 2,500 yuan, which were supported by corresponding evidence and constitute reasonable expenses for Shenzhen [a certain] Technology Co., Ltd. to protect its rights. This Court supports such claim.

In summary, based on the facts further ascertained in the second instance, this Court adjusts the amount of compensation determined in the first instance judgment as follows: Shenzhen [a certain] Electronic Technology Co., Ltd. and Luo shall jointly and severally compensate Shenzhen [a certain] Technology Co., Ltd. for economic losses of 7,500 yuan and reasonable expenses of 2,500 yuan, totaling 10,000 yuan.

(IV) Regarding the enforcement of this judgment

It should be pointed out that the patent-in-suit is a utility model patent, which has not undergone substantive examination. Filing a request for invalidation of a utility model patent right is an important defense for the accused infringer. Where the administrative procedure for patent invalidation is suspended due to the adoption of property preservation measures against the patent-in-suit, resulting in the inability to render an invalidation review decision before the second-instance judgment in the patent infringement lawsuit, the people's court may, based on the specific circumstances of the case, make corresponding arrangements for the enforcement of the second-instance judgment, including attaching necessary conditions to the enforcement of judgments such as cessation of infringement and compensation for losses, in order to reasonably balance the interests of all parties. Although the property preservation of the patent-in-suit was caused by a dispute between the patentee and a third party, from the perspective of the legal relationship between the patentee and the accused infringer, it is clear that the responsibility for timely lifting the property preservation lies with the patentee, and the accused infringer should not be made to bear the possible adverse consequences. At the same time, the people's court must also prevent the occurrence of dishonest conduct such as malicious suspension of the patent invalidation administrative procedure due to the patentee's own reasons.

Considering this Court's aforementioned determination regarding the prior art defense, and the fact that a third party, [a certain] Investment Company and Dongguan [a certain] Electronic Technology Co., Ltd., have already raised specific invalidation grounds and evidence against claim 8 of the patent-in-suit in the patent invalidation administrative procedure, there is a high possibility that claim 8 of the patent-in-suit will be declared invalid. The determination of the invalidation review decision regarding the patent-in-suit may have a significant impact on the trial of the relevant civil infringement case and the enforcement of this judgment. More importantly, Shenzhen [a certain] Technology Co., Ltd. holds 17 valid patents in its name, and solely due to its own reasons, through the relevant content of a mediation document, it unreasonably delayed the property preservation measures against the patent-in-suit until 2026, rendering the invalidation administrative procedure for the patent-in-suit unable to proceed, which will inevitably cause a significant imbalance of interests between the parties in this case. Such conduct by Shenzhen [a certain] Technology Co., Ltd. is clearly unreasonable and violates the principle of good faith, and cannot be accepted by this Court. Therefore, this Court makes the issuance of a review decision by the China National Intellectual Property Administration (CNIPA) upholding the validity of the patent claim on which Shenzhen [a certain] Technology Co., Ltd. based its lawsuit a prerequisite for the enforcement of this second-instance judgment, and makes arrangements for the interest during the period as follows:

First, before the CNIPA issues a review decision upholding the validity of claim 8 of the patent-in-suit in response to the invalidation request, Shenzhen [a certain] Electronic Technology Co., Ltd. and Luo may temporarily refrain from performing the obligations of ceasing the infringement and compensating for losses determined in this judgment.

Second, after the CNIPA issues a review decision upholding the validity of claim 8 of the patent-in-suit in response to the invalidation request, Shenzhen [a certain] Technology Co., Ltd. shall immediately notify Shenzhen [a certain] Electronic Technology Co., Ltd. and Luo of such review decision. Upon receipt of the notice, Shenzhen [a certain] Electronic Technology Co., Ltd. and Luo shall immediately perform the judgment item of ceasing the infringement determined in this judgment, and shall perform the monetary payment obligation determined in this judgment within seven days from the date of notice.

Third, from the date this judgment is served on Shenzhen [a certain] Electronic Technology Co., Ltd. and Luo to the date on which Shenzhen [a certain] Electronic Technology Co., Ltd. and Luo perform the monetary payment obligation determined in this judgment within seven days from the date of notice by Shenzhen [a certain] Technology Co., Ltd. in accordance with the preceding paragraph, Shenzhen [a certain] Electronic Technology Co., Ltd. and Luo shall pay interest calculated at the loan prime rate (LPR) for the same period published by the National Interbank Funding Center. If Shenzhen [a certain] Electronic Technology Co., Ltd. and Luo fail to perform the monetary payment obligation determined in this judgment within seven days from the date of receipt of the notice from Shenzhen [a certain] Technology Co., Ltd., they shall, in accordance with Article 264 of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC, pay double the interest on the debt for the period of delayed performance.

Fourth, if the CNIPA issues a review decision declaring claim 8 of the patent-in-suit invalid in response to the invalidation request, and such review decision has become legally effective, this judgment shall no longer be enforced.
